# The Cairn System: Core Concepts

## Pulses
A pulse makes a cairn grow by adding two components:
1. The stride (a fixed amount per cairn)
2. A bonus equal to how many complete strides fit into the current height

This means taller cairns grow more from each pulse because they contain more complete strides. When applying multiple pulses in a row, you must recalculate the bonus each time since the height changes after every pulse.

## Leaks
A leak removes marks after a pulse happens. The amount removed depends on the leak size: you divide the new height (after pulsing) by the leak size and remove marks equal to the whole number result. The leak always works with the post-pulse height, not the starting height.

## Drains
A drain is simpler than a leak—it removes a fixed number of marks after each pulse. When repeatedly applying pulse-and-drain cycles, the cairn may stabilize at a certain height or eventually reach zero, depending on how much the pulse adds versus what the drain removes.

## Finding Origins
To find what height a cairn started at before pulses were applied, you work backwards. For each pulse you undo, you solve for the previous height by finding the value that, when pulsed, produces the current height. You cannot simply subtract; you must reverse each pulse individually because pulse amounts vary with height.

## Merging
When combining two cairns, you calculate a weighted blend using shares (which sum to 1), apply a tether scaling factor to the shorter cairn's height, and sum everything together. The tether can be positive or negative and significantly affects the result.
